writing.overall_comment: Strong domain content in the opening sections, but the file needs deduplication, placeholder removal, and an explicit boundary/output contract before it is production-ready.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: Description clearly signals an iOS/SwiftUI specialist tied to relevant skills, so routing is feasible, though it lacks explicit 'use when' triggers to distinguish it from a generic Swift agent.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, stack, principles, and workflow are concrete with good ✅/❌ examples, but there is no output contract (deliverable format/summary expectations) and large portions remain unfilled template placeholders.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: Some 'Don'ts' exist, but there is no statement of scope limits (e.g., non-iOS platforms, backend/DevOps work) or conditions for handing back to the main agent.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The useful first half is undercut by duplicated 'Best Practices' and 'Quality Checklist' sections plus empty placeholder blocks that burn tokens without adding guidance.

suggestions: In the skill file, remove the duplicated Best Practices and Quality Checklist sections and empty placeholder blocks to save tokens and sharpen guidance.
In the Boundaries section, add explicit scope limits for non-iOS platforms and backend/DevOps work, along with clear handback conditions for the main agent.

In the prompt/skill instructions, add an output contract specifying deliverable format and summary expectations, and add explicit 'use when' triggers to the description to distinguish it from a generic Swift agent.
